catalog_quote: Stress is usually not indicated, since it regularly falls on the penultimate syllable in all Tomini-Tolitoli languages. Only the exceptions to this rule are marked. Primary stress is marked by an acute accent <´>, secondary stress (i.e. lengthening of reduplicated syllables) by a grave accent (`). Most exceptions to the general stress rule are well-motivated (either a phonetically long vowel is shortened (cf. §3.4.6 above) or stress moves to the first member of a sequence of unlike vowels as in táipang 'mango', which occurs as an alternate to the regular taípang). In Balaesang, however, stress also occurs on final short closed syllables as in moontol [montól] 'sharp'. This includes syllables which are closed by a non-phonemic glottal stop, e.g. ita pronounced as [itá'] 'we (exclusive)'. ... [§3.4.6] In the southern Tomini languages, there is an additional strategy for avoiding phonetica…

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation is verbatim at the stated place in the held printed p.73 = PDF p.95, sec. 3.4.8). (2) Deciding source: Himmelmann 2001 is a wordlist sourcebook whose introduction gives a group-wide penultimate-stress statement plus a Balaesang-specific note (final stress on some short closed syllables), by the field phonologist of record for the group; the only dedicated description of Balaesang, the 1985 Pusat Bahasa sketch Struktur Bahasa Balaesang, is also held and its sec. 2.5-2.6 (pp.16-18, page images read because p.16 has no text layer) independently states regular, predictable, non-phonemic penultimate accent that stays penultimate under suffixation. Both existing descriptive sources in Glottolog's bibliography are therefore held and agree with the classification 'fixed penultimate, exceptions lexically marked'. (3) Nothing better exists that we lack:

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: 'Stress placement is very regular in Tomini-Tolitoli languages and thus empirically defines the domain of (word) phonology. It falls on the penultimate syllable of a (phonological) word and 'remains' penultimate when suffixes or clitics are added. ... Exceptions to this rule are very few in number' (secs. 2.2-2.5: Lauje paragogic vowel keeps antepenult stress; final long vowels; ultima stress after clitic-vowel drop; antepenult stress in non-high+high vowel sequences e.g. táipang). The 1991 sample is Taje, Tajio, Lauje, Tialo, Boano, Pendau, Dampelas, Dampal, Dondo, Totoli; Balaesang is not me
sources.locator: sec. 2.1 'Stress', printed p.51 (PDF p.3); language list p.49
sources.note: The group-level phonology article behind the Sourcebook's stress note; downloaded and read: confirms penultimate stress for the Tomini-Tolitoli group but Balaesang is outside its 1991 sample, so it adds only background to this record.
